login.title: Log in to Particle
login.description:
{why}

Your Particle login is only used during this setup: Home Assistant creates an API user limited to one product (list devices, read variables, call functions, read and publish events) and stores only that user's token. The login token is deleted at the end.

mfa.title: Two-step verification
mfa.description: Enter the code from your authenticator app.

device.title: Device
device.description: Pick a device ({count} on the account). The next step asks which product it should be in. More devices of the same product can be added later under Configure.

product.title: Product for {device}
product.description:
{current} Home Assistant's API user is scoped to one product. Keep the device where it is, or move it to another {platform} product (only products of the device's platform are listed) (existing or new): it is removed from its current product and added to the new one. If the target product has released firmware, the device is marked as a development device so that firmware won't replace yours.

{error}

error.invalid_auth: Particle didn't accept that email and password.
error.invalid_otp: That code didn't work. Codes change every 30 s; try the current one.
error.not_product_admin: That device is in a product you can't manage with this login. Pick another device.
error.product_failed: Particle refused the product step (see below).
error.name_required: Give the new product a name.
error.incompatible_product: That product is for another platform; pick one made for this device's platform.

abort.already_configured: This product is already set up and already has this device.
abort.device_added: This product was already set up; the device has been added to it.
abort.api_user_failed: Particle refused to create the API user.
abort.reauth_successful: New API user created; the old one was deleted.
abort.reconfigure_successful: Switched to the new API user; the old access was removed.

devices.title: Devices in {product}
devices.description: Pick the devices Home Assistant should see. Cloud variables are read every poll interval (a cloud round trip each, which uses data on cellular devices); prefer `ha/` events for live values.

login.title: Revoke Particle access
login.description:
{why}

The entry and its entities stay; it will ask to re-authenticate.

mfa.title: Two-step verification
mfa.description: Enter the code from your authenticator app.

error.invalid_auth: Particle didn't accept that email and password.
error.invalid_otp: That code didn't work. Codes change every 30 s; try the current one.

abort.invalid_auth: The API user's token was rejected. Re-authenticate the integration.
abort.revoke_failed: Particle refused to delete the API user; check the product's Team page.
abort.revoked: API user deleted. The integration now waits for re-authentication (Reconfigure or the re-authenticate prompt).

stream_down.title: Particle event stream down
stream_down.description: Home Assistant hasn't had a working Particle event stream for over {minutes} minutes, so device events and `ha/` sensors aren't updating. It keeps reconnecting by itself. Last error: {error}

call_function.name: Call function
call_function.description: Call a cloud function on a Particle device. Returns its integer return value.

publish_event.name: Publish event
publish_event.description: Publish an event into every Particle product set up in Home Assistant; their devices receive it with Particle.subscribe().
